note: Each case is a complete manifest document plus the single diagnostic code it must produce. Cases live here rather than in one directory each because every one of them is a *document* defect; only the bundle/ cases need real files on disk.

cases.name: root-not-an-object
cases.why: A manifest that is not an object has no grammar at all, so nothing later can be interpreted.

cases.name: format-version-missing
cases.why: Without a declared format version the reader would have to guess which grammar applies.

cases.name: format-version-unsupported
cases.why: A future major version must be refused with the observed value and the supported range, never partially interpreted.

cases.name: section-missing
cases.why: policy is omitted. The perimeter and the outbound bounds have no safe default, so the manifest cannot load without it.

cases.name: section-unknown
cases.why: An unknown section name is usually a misspelling of a real one. Ignoring it would silently drop whatever the author intended it to configure.

cases.name: section-both-inline-and-path
cases.why: Two payload sources for one section leave the effective content ambiguous, and a reader that silently prefers one would let the other be a decoy.

cases.name: section-neither-inline-nor-path
cases.why: An entry with no payload source is a declaration with nothing behind it.

cases.name: section-must-be-external
cases.why: The vector matrix is a binary payload outside the determinism contract; admitting it inline would put unbounded base64 inside the document the seal covers.

cases.name: root-unknown-member
cases.why: An unrecognised root member is either a typo or an attempt to smuggle configuration past a strict reader.

cases.name: inline-payload-with-digest
cases.why: A digest on an inline payload is a second authority over bytes that already sit inside the sealed document, with no independent writer to disagree with.

cases.name: section-unknown-member
cases.why: A misspelled policy member would otherwise silently fall back to a default perimeter the author did not intend.

cases.name: section-not-an-object
cases.why: A section payload of the wrong JSON kind has no members to read.

cases.name: operations-duplicate-key
cases.why: The execution key is the address a binding resolves. Two operations sharing it would make the executed request depend on declaration order.

cases.name: operations-key-disagrees
cases.why: A key that disagrees with the method and path it claims to address would let the advertised operation and the executed request diverge.

cases.name: operations-querystring-parameter
cases.why: The intermediate model has a querystring location but the request compiler refuses it, so admitting it here would create an authorable but unexecutable operation.

cases.name: operations-unknown-style
cases.why: An unknown serialization style has no defined wire behavior, and falling back to the default would silently change the request shape.

cases.name: schema-ref-not-local
cases.why: A non-local reference would turn manifest loading into a network fetch, which the format deliberately cannot do.

cases.name: schema-ref-unresolvable
cases.why: A dangling pointer must be reported at load, not discovered as an empty schema during the first invocation.

cases.name: schema-ref-cycle
cases.why: A reference chain that never reaches a schema is unresolvable rather than a bound violation, so the message names the cycle instead of blaming the depth limit.

cases.name: surface-duplicate-slug
cases.why: The slug is the route segment. Two surfaces sharing it would make the served catalogue depend on declaration order.

cases.name: surface-no-default
cases.why: Without a default surface the unqualified route has nothing to resolve to.

cases.name: surface-multiple-defaults
cases.why: Two defaults make the unqualified route ambiguous, and picking the first would let declaration order decide which catalogue is served.

cases.name: surface-operation-unknown
cases.why: A surface entry naming an operation that does not exist is a dangling grant; refusing it keeps the exposure list the single runtime authority.

cases.name: surface-duplicate-operation
cases.why: The same operation listed twice with different exposures would let declaration order decide whether it is advertised.

cases.name: agent-duplicate-slug
cases.why: The slug is the manifest-local identity used by surfaces, compound steps and derived sections. Duplicates make every one of those references ambiguous.

cases.name: agent-unknown-group
cases.why: Group membership joins by name. An undeclared name is a typo that would otherwise silently drop the operation out of its group.

cases.name: agent-kind-binding-mismatch
cases.why: A declared kind that contradicts the binding shape would let the two disagree about what actually executes.

cases.name: binding-operation-key-unknown
cases.why: A binding naming a key with no operation behind it is an advertised tool that can never execute.

cases.name: binding-compound-nested
cases.why: Nesting a compound inside a compound removes the single-level bound on how much work one invocation can start.

cases.name: binding-compound-step-unknown-operation
cases.why: A step referencing a slug that does not exist is a workflow that fails partway through after earlier steps have already run.

cases.name: binding-duplicate-step-id
cases.why: Step identifiers address step outputs. Duplicates would let declaration order decide which response a later mapping reads.

cases.name: binding-step-reference-unknown
cases.why: A step reading its own response, or a later step's, describes a workflow that can never execute in the declared order.

cases.name: policy-base-url-invalid
cases.why: The base URL seeds the default perimeter, so an unparseable value must refuse the section rather than produce an empty one.

cases.name: policy-origin-invalid
cases.why: An origin carrying a path implies a narrower permission than the origin comparison actually applies, so accepting and truncating it would record a perimeter the operator did not authorise.

cases.name: policy-destination-not-allowed
cases.why: A per-operation server URL outside the perimeter is refused at load, because it can never widen the perimeter at execution time and would otherwise fail on every call.

cases.name: credential-scheme-unknown
cases.why: No applier branch matches an unknown scheme, so accepting it would produce a credential that is silently never sent.

cases.name: credential-slot-duplicate
cases.why: One binding reaching two credentials that write the same header makes the value actually sent depend on declaration order.

cases.name: credential-slot-invalid
cases.why: A basic credential missing one half produces an Authorization header built from a value the author never supplied.

cases.name: credential-inline-not-permitted
cases.why: A literal secret in the manifest is refused unless the operator opts in, because a manifest is a file that gets copied, committed and shipped in images.

cases.name: credential-id-missing
cases.why: A credential with no identifier is unreachable from any binding, and under the fail-safe default an unreachable credential is never applied at all.

cases.name: credential-id-invalid
cases.why: Upper case is refused rather than folded, because folding would let two declarations that differ only by case become one identifier.

cases.name: credential-duplicate-id
cases.why: Two credentials answering to one identifier make the credential a binding actually reaches depend on declaration order, which is the ambiguity the identifier exists to remove.

cases.name: binding-credential-ref-unknown
cases.why: A dangling reference is the failure mode that silently applies nothing, so it is refused rather than tolerated as an empty scope.

cases.name: binding-credential-basic-incomplete
cases.why: Basic authentication composes one header from two slots, so a binding that reaches only one of them would send a credential no upstream service can accept.

cases.name: credential-ref-on-a-transformed-wrapper
cases.why: The base is the operation that actually runs, so a scope stated on the wrapper would be silently ignored and the binding would look authorized when it is not.

cases.name: credential-ref-on-a-compound-binding
cases.why: A compound binding has no request of its own, so its steps carry the scope; accepting one here would describe a credential that reaches nothing.

cases.name: authentication-kind-unknown
cases.why: An unknown kind cannot select a closed configuration schema, so nothing about the profile can be validated.

cases.name: authentication-kind-not-executable
cases.why: The kind is in the vocabulary so a stored value round-trips, but no accepted artifact defines its runtime semantics, so accepting it would defer the failure to the first invocation. The sections declare the current versions so the refusal pins the kind rule rather than the version gate.

cases.name: authentication-id-invalid
cases.why: A profile id is the manifest-local identity a binding references; it shares the credential charset so one identity rule covers the format.
